title: Vendor Onboarding - MSA & DPA Review
summary: Redwood AE/SE reviewed MSA/DPA terms, SLA targets, pricing approval path, and vendor onboarding requirements. Customer requested redlines on liability/indemnity, data residency clarifications, subprocessor list, and PO/billing cadence. Agreed next steps: send redlined MSA, security pack, pricing spreadsheet, and schedule legal follow-up next week.
next_steps: Sophie to send draft redlined MSA and DPA by 2025-02-03
Liam to attach security pack (SOC2 report, ISO certs, subprocessors) and KMS architecture doc
Jordan to confirm procurement timeline and PO terms (net-30 vs net-45) by 2025-02-05
action_items: Sophie: Send redlined MSA/DPA and pricing spreadsheet (due 2025-02-03)
Liam: Share security pack, SOC2 summary, subprocessor list, KMS/HSM integration notes (due 2025-02-03)
Jordan: Provide PO requirements and internal approver list (due 2025-02-05)
Maya: Provide initial redlines on indemnity and liability caps ahead of legal sync (due 2025-02-04)
transcript:
[00:00] Meeting header: 2025-01-28 16:00 PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Sophie Chen, Liam Ortiz (Redwood); Maya Patel, Jordan Rivers, Dr. Kevin Huang (Atlas)
[00:10] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick roll call?
[00:15] Maya: yes hi Maya here, head of legal at Atlas, hi
[00:18] Jordan: Jordan, procurement
[00:20] Kevin: Kevin, CTO, hello
[00:22] Sophie: and Sophie from Redwood, AE, and Liam our SE is on too. thanks for carving time, we know this is legal/procurement heavy so happy to go deep.
[00:36] Liam: yeah hi all, I can cover security and architecture bits when we hit DPA and subprocessors.
[00:40] Maya: ideal. main goals today: understand liability/indemnity language, subprocessor transparency, data residency, and clarify SLAs and credits. we also need to map procurement steps for PO and pricing approval.
[00:52] Sophie: perfect. i'll start with the MSA high level — we shared a baseline earlier this week, it's the standard redwood MSA; key negotiables we've seen are liability caps, indemnities, termination for convenience, and data processing terms.
[01:06] Jordan: on procurement side we need payment terms (net-30 vs net-45), invoice cadence, and PO wording. Atlas requires vendor onboarding questionnaire and SOC2 or ISO attestation.
[01:18] Liam: we have a SOC2 type II from 2024, ISO27001 cert linked in the security pack; subprocessors list is included but it's a snapshot — we can provide a current list and commit to notice before new subprocessors on enterprise agreements.
[01:30] Maya: on DPA, data residency is key — some PHI-adjacent workloads need EU residency for EU patients; can Redwood guarantee that?
[01:40] Liam: for hosted API we have region routing and EU-hosted deployments; for stricter needs we offer Redwood Private with VPC and on-prem options. the private offering can ensure data never leaves the customer's region.
[01:55] Kevin: technical question — for private, what's key management flow? do you support customer-managed KMS or bring-your-own-key?
[02:02] Liam: yes, customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or Cloud HSM in private deployments; for Hosted we encrypt at rest and we can integrate with customer KMS for enterprise contracts — details in the KMS doc.
[02:15] Jordan: procurement also wants to know SLA numbers — uptime, p99 latency targets, and credits methodology.
[02:22] Sophie: our standard SLA is 99.9% for hosted API, with credits for downtime, and dedicated/dedicated-reserved capacity has stronger SLOs in the contract. the SLA clause in the MSA spells out measurement windows and credit calculation, but we can discuss tailoring for enterprise.
[02:35] Maya: indemnity — we need mutual indemnities for third-party claims, exceptions around gross negligence and willful misconduct, but the customer-side liability cap in your baseline seemed low.
[02:45] Sophie: understood. historically we negotiate liability cap to a multiple of annual fees; we can provide options (e.g., 1x, 3x, or an unlimited cap for IP infringement). we try to avoid unlimited caps for general liability but will work through specifics.
[02:57] Maya: and what about data breach notification timelines? our policy is 72 hours.
[03:02] Liam: we commit to 72 hours for confirmed breaches; we have incident response and forensic support — security pack has runbook excerpt.
[03:10] Jordan: on billing, do you accept consolidated monthly invoices? do you require net-30 after delivery of services or after invoice date? our AP needs clear PO references.
[03:20] Sophie: we support monthly consolidated invoices referencing PO numbers; net-30 from invoice date is typical but open to net-45 depending on enterprise procurement.
[03:25] Jordan: ok we'll confirm internal approvers.
[03:30] [00:03:30] Liam: quick note — subprocessors: we use cloud infra providers (AWS/GCP), monitoring vendors, and a model-hosting infra partner; all listed in the subprocessor sheet, can provide SOC2 for each on request where available.
[03:45] Maya: please include any international transfer mechanisms for EU data — standard contractual clauses or EU SCCs?
[03:50] Liam: we can include SCCs and we offer data processing addendum that references SCCs by default for EU customers. for Private deployments transfers are unnecessary.
[04:05] Sophie: for timeline, what is Atlas's internal procurement cadence? Jordan?
[04:10] Jordan: procurement approval takes 2-3 weeks once legal signs off; pricing needs business approval from product lead and finance, might be another week. overall target to be onboarded within ~6 weeks if no major redlines.
[04:24] Maya: we will need a marked-up MSA to circulate internally, with suggested language on indemnity and liability. can you provide redlines?
[04:30] Sophie: yes we'll send a redlined MSA and DPA by next Monday (2025-02-03) — that'll include alternate liability caps and suggested indemnity wording.
[04:40] [00:04:40] Kevin: about SLA credits, do credits offset fees automatically or do we need to claim?
[04:44] Sophie: credits are issued after an SLA claim process — customer submits an incident claim and we validate, then issue service credits applied to next invoice. we can add auto-crediting for severe outages as a negotiated term.
[04:55] Maya: also need to confirm retention and deletion policy — how long logs, prompts, and outputs are retained?
[05:00] Liam: by default logs and request traces are retained 90 days; prompt/response retention for hosted can be configured per contract — for enterprise we can set retention windows or opt-out of storage. this will be documented in the DPA.
[05:15] Jordan: can Redwood provide a vendor security questionnaire filled or do you expect us to use our own?
[05:20] Sophie: we can fill vendor questionnaires and have a templated answers pack; faster to share our security pack and SOC2, but we'll also fill a vendor questionnaire if you send one.
[05:30] Maya: subprocessors: is there a commitment on notice period before adding a new subprocessor?
[05:35] Liam: typical enterprise term is 30 days notice before new subprocessor goes live or we notify and give opt-out rights in rare cases; we can include a 30-day notice clause.
[05:45] [00:05:45] Sophie: pricing — have you had a chance to review the enterprise pricing spreadsheet?
[05:50] Jordan: yes we've seen it, pricing will need executive sign-off; what's the path for getting discounts locked in?
[05:56] Sophie: discounts are tied to commit levels and contract term — multi-year or reserved committed capacity (Dedicated) get steeper discounts. we'll send a final pricing sheet with contract-level terms.
[06:08] Maya: liability carve-outs — we need specific carve-outs for regulatory fines arising from customer misuse of data?
[06:15] Sophie: generally liabilities arising from customer misuse remain customer's responsibility; we can add language to that effect.
[06:20] Maya: good. also, any change to the DPA around subprocessors or new data types requires notice.
[06:25] Liam: yes, DPA will have notification flows and subprocessor list with last-updated timestamp.
[06:30] Jordan: how do you handle background checks for personnel with access to production data?
[06:36] Liam: we perform standard employee background checks, role-based access controls, and limited production access; documented in security pack.
[06:42] [00:06:42] Sophie: ok let's surface the typical redlines we expect — i'll read them so legal can follow: increase liability cap to X multiple, mutual indemnity for IP, 30-day notice for subprocessors, 72-hour breach notification, PO/payment net-30 by default, support SLA to be 99.9% or enterprise tier.
[06:58] Maya: on IP indemnity, we may ask for seller to defend IP claims but want clarity on process and control of defense.
[07:05] Sophie: we can negotiate defense control and carveouts; often we propose vendor controls defense with cooperation obligations.
[07:12] Kevin: any mention of performance benchmarks? we may ask for sample p99 latency numbers for our workload size.
[07:18] Liam: we can run a short benchmark — SE-led perf run using a sample prompt set, and we provide p50/p95/p99 numbers for hosted vs dedicated. that can be done as a PoC or as a pre-contract benchmark.
[07:30] Jordan: procurement will want acceptance criteria for onboarding — what defines successful onboarding?
[07:35] Sophie: onboarding checklist: security review passed, billing/PO processed, staging keys provisioned, integration test passed (latency/throughput), and runbook and SLAs acknowledged. typical onboarding 2-4 weeks.
[07:47] Maya: contracts team typically wants language for audit rights — can Redwood accommodate audits or provide audit reports?
[07:52] Liam: we provide audit reports (SOC2) and can accommodate on-site or third-party audits under NDA and scheduled windows for enterprise customers.
[08:03] Sophie: i want to confirm the documents we'll send: redlined MSA + DPA, pricing spreadsheet, security pack (SOC2/ISO/subprocessors), and benchmark proposal. any additions?
[08:12] Maya: please include SCCs and explicit data residency language for EU patients.
[08:16] Sophie: noted.
[08:20] [00:08:20] Jordan: a couple of small things: will Redwood accept standard Atlas SLA exclusions (force majeure) and insurance requirements?
[08:28] Sophie: yes we have insurance certificate and our standard MSA includes force majeure; if you need higher limits we can discuss.
[08:34] Maya: also need to confirm privacy/security contact for Data Processing Amendments.
[08:38] Liam: liam@redwood.example.com is our security contact; we can include a dedicated SOC/SEA contact in the pack.
[08:47] Kevin: about dedicated capacity — if we move to dedicated GPUs for inference, do you offer on-prem or only cloud-hosted dedicated?
[08:55] Liam: Dedicated is available as reserved capacity in cloud regions, Private (VPC/on-prem) is available for stricter requirements; both are supported but on-prem incurs additional ops fees.
[09:05] Maya: we will also want to know data deletion certification process at termination — can you provide a cert of deletion?
[09:12] Liam: we can provide deletion confirmation and documented procedures; for Private deployments customers can control the deletion themselves.
[09:20] [00:09:20] Sophie: great, any last-minute redlines we should expect?
[09:23] Maya: indemnity and liability cap + SCCs + data residency; nothing else major.
[09:28] Jordan: procurement will follow up with PO process doc.
[09:30] Sophie: ok recap: we'll send redlined MSA/DPA, security pack, pricing, benchmark proposal; you (Atlas) will review and provide preliminary redlines and PO requirements. legal-only sync proposed next week.
[09:45] Maya: sounds good. thanks Sophie and Liam.
[09:48] Sophie: thanks all — we'll target sending materials by 2025-02-03, and schedule legal sync for 2025-02-06 pending confirmations.
[09:55] [00:09:55] End of call.
